history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this row ('Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple', Geyzing) is a CONFIRMED DUPLICATE of CSV row 916 - there is only ONE famous Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple, at Legship in Gyalshing district on the Rangeet river; no separate Kirateshwar Mahadev temple at Geyzing town was found in any source. Geyzing is the district HQ (~15 km away) and some travel sites describe the temple as easily visited from Geyzing, which likely explains the CSV town. Row 916 covers this temple; deprecate this row or keep with cross-reference. One of Sikkim's few genuinely Hindu temples, standing on the Rangeet riverbank at Legship, ~4 km from Pelling on the Geyzing-Pelling route, reached via a footbridge. Legend: pleased with Arjuna's hard penance, Lord Shiva appeared here as the hunter Kirateshwar ('Lord of the Kiratas') and blessed him for the Mahabharata war; a stone miraculously manifesting a Shiv Lingam was later found, and this swayambhu lingam is the main object of worship. Devotees believe a visit with true devotion fulfils wishes - notably for children - and grants peace, health and harmony. Also known as Kirateshwar Mahadev Thaan to the Kirati people; smaller shrines to Rama and Durga stand in the complex. A guest house for devotees stands on site.

name: Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple
town: Legship, Gyalshing district (CSV town 'Geyzing' is approximate - the temple is at Legship, ~15 km from Geyzing; no separate temple at Geyzing found)
town_description: Legship is a small town on the Rangeet river in Gyalshing district, West Sikkim, on the Geyzing-Pelling tourist route (~4 km from Pelling). The temple sits below the main road on the riverbank, reached by a footbridge and steps; the river setting and forested hills make it one of Sikkim's most scenic pilgrimage spots.

travel.airport: Pakyong Airport - about 100 km (verify); Siliguri/Bagdogra is the main air gateway.
travel.road: Day trip from Pelling (~4 km) or Geyzing (~15 km); footbridge from the main road to the temple; local taxis and shared vehicles (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; avoid monsoon (river access can be risky). Bala Chaturdashi (Nov-Dec) is the grandest but crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Widely reported as 6:00 AM-7:00 PM (verify). Daily Vedic puja with morning/evening aarti; dress modestly, remove footwear before the sanctum.
